title: This blog has a message
content:
I have a plan for how to bootstrap WordLand 0.8.

First I will introduce you to a new way to read my blog.

It will be a timeline of items posted to many of my feeds.

  • daveverse -- lives on WordPress and Mastodon.
  • Great art on Bluesky -- daily version.
  • links.daveverse.org -- my linkblog.
  • Scripting News -- my main blog.
  • Scripting News podcast -- a new podcast stream.
  • WordCamp Canada 2025 -- I'm keynoting in October.

Some people read my stuff and not the rest of it. There is no one place where you can get All-of-Dave, but there will be soon.

We haven't yet set things up so we do all our writing in one place and that can flow in to many different contexts.

  • A great example would have been Substack. I wanted to hook up a feed to their newsletter publishing system. I don't like being a copy/paste machine. This is what I mean about being on the web. It's like pipes in Unix. The output of one app is the input to another. It's how we build systems. On the web everything you think of works.

This is simmering debate in our world, what is the web? I think if you can't plug your output into their input, it's not the web.

Anyway... so instead of going to scripting.com, you'll go to this other place, on an experimental basis. If you don't like it, all the individual feeds are still where they are. You can read daveverse on Mastodon or WordPress. Great art is on Bluesky. The linkblog is all over the place. The podcast is on your podcast player. And my posts on WordCamp Canada are on their site, and they promote the stuff nicely, so you may pick it up on other places.

What each of these have in common is that each has an RSS feed that supports rssCloud. So updates flow instantaneously.

Now here's the fun part. You may read something that you're just dying to comment on. Or quote what I've said. The kinds of things you do on twitter-like systems.

You will be able to do that. The editor is right there. One click away while you're reading. I didn't invent this flow, Twitter did, it's comfortable, we understand it.

The difference is here you edit in your space and pass around links.

How do you pass around the links?

Really Simple Syndication! :-)

This, my friends, imho, is how the web has always wanted social media to work.

PS: My timeline as a FeedLand-compatible reading list.
